bounds.rationale: Two frames give at least one retire-then-restart cycle, so the budget-monotone property and the per-frame reset of the allocation accounting are both exercised.
Java's fixed control-payload limit, used verbatim rather than a scaled-down stand-in, so the gate comparisons run against the real constant.
The port's default max_frame_payload_bytes (rust/ws-core/src/config.rs LimitField::MaxFramePayloadBytes), used verbatim.

One bit per octet on the mask track. XOR acts independently per bit position, so the reduced domain is exact for the involution and key-alignment properties; the module's ASSUME separately checks the full two-bit XOR table exhaustively.
Longer than the four-octet mask key, so the key index wraps and a misalignment mutation is detectable.

findings.statement: The shipped port checks the 125-octet control-payload limit twice: it rejects any control frame whose length marker is >= 126 at header byte 2, and it separately compares the decoded payload length against 125 at the length site. The second comparison is UNREACHABLE, because a control frame that survives the first gate has an inline marker and therefore a length of at most 125. TLC confirms this mechanically: ControlOverLimitRejectedAtBaseHeader holds, so every over-limit control frame is rejected at consumed offset 2. The shipped Java gate has the same shape (drafts/Draft_6455.java:617-620), so the port's second comparison is defensive depth that matches the fidelity authority.

The checker contradicted the author, in attempt us007-sbx-output-live-0127. The declared key-index mutation SURVIVED the original MaskRoundTrip invariant with exit 0 over the identical 3,618-state space: XOR with any fixed index function is an involution, so a round-trip-only check is blind to key ALIGNMENT and the invariant was partially vacuous with a wrong falsification note. The fix is in the MODEL: the mask equation is restated independently as MaskEquationReference and the invariant checks the transform against it. In attempt 0128 that same mutation is killed with exit 12. The port's mask function was never in question; the defect was in the check. This finding is the reason every check in both models now carries an EXECUTED mutation rather than a declared one.

An EVIDENCE-PIPELINE defect, not a model or port defect. TLC reports a [][...]_vars ACTION property violation as 'Error: Action property X is violated', a third message form distinct from the state-invariant and temporal-property forms. The driver's first classification pass in this attempt (sandbox us012-us016-tlc-0128b) knew only the first two and therefore labelled three GENUINE kills -- FrameBudgetMonotone, TerminalAbsorbing, PoisonAbsorbing -- as SURVIVORS, while their checker exit codes said 13. It was caught by reading the raw checker output rather than trusting the classifier's summary, and the same gap was present in the results validator's binder and fixed there too. Had the summary been believed, this record would have understated the kill table by three and reported three false survivors.

honesty_notes: Claim ceiling proved-model, full stop. This run establishes properties of an ABSTRACTION and nothing about production Rust without a reviewed composition/refinement link.

OWNER_ATTESTED_NOT_INDEPENDENT: one session authored the model, the invariants, the mutations, and this record, and ran the checker. Two vacuous checks have already been found in this lane -- one by the checker, one by a reviewer -- so the correlated-failure risk is demonstrated, not hypothetical.

NON-VACUITY IS NOW COMPLETE FOR THIS MODEL, and that phrasing is exact: every invariant and every property in the shipped cfg has ONE seeded mutation that was EXECUTED and killed it, with the killing check read out of the checker's own output. That is stronger than attempt 0127, where most falsification notes were declared but never run -- and where two of the unexecuted ones turned out to be wrong. It is NOT a claim that the checks are complete: a mutation set proves the checks can fail, never that they would catch every possible defect.

The attempt used three sandbox instantiations under one attempt id. That contradicts the series' one-sandbox-per-attempt-id pattern and this attempt's own authorization text, and the output bytes of the two non-published sandboxes were NOT retained. Both are self-reported constraint violations, recorded in protected/us012-us016-attempt-0128-correction-sandbox-reconciliation.json rather than smoothed over. The lost artifacts are not reconstructed; the failures they recorded are reproducible from the committed commits instead. Stated exactly, per correction-2: source-level reproduction establishes the DEFECT CLASSES at those commits, NOT that those executions happened -- for the two non-published sandboxes a reader must take the prose on trust. Only the published sandbox is independently auditable.

The model is bounded. MaxFrames = 2 and the four length classes mean the checked results hold only for behaviors inside those bounds; lengths strictly between the class representatives are not enumerated.

The two-track structure means the decode obligations and the mask obligations were checked in the SAME run but over DISJOINT state spaces. Nothing here checks their composition -- that an accepted masked frame's payload is the one that gets unmasked -- and no such claim is made.
